title: Statistical Coincidence Suppression for Energy-Dispersive X-Ray Spectroscopy using Pulse Width Modulation
content: Coincidence loss is a well-known problem that limits data throughput in energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDX). Every microscopist who has performed EDX is familiar with dead time and the need to sometimes reduce beam current to keep the signal rate within the bandwidth of the detection system. If two photons arrive within one “process time” T of each other, both must be discarded, as the circuitry that integrates pulse amplitude to determine photon energy can’t separate the two (Fig. 1A). While one can often reduce the process time, this comes at the cost of energy resolution and may limit the precision of compositional analysis. Even a modest improvement of the tradeoff curve between precision and throughput would be useful for many users.
